comparisons.finding: Strongest long-reading composition. Dedicated heading establishes context; minimal reader overhead and a bottom return support completion at 200%. Index rows remain legible. Switching sections requires returning to the index.
Selector is compact, but hides available sections and gives the page title weak emphasis. At the long reason's 200% bottom, neither selector nor return is visible. Body text itself wraps cleanly.

Disclosure arrows clearly distinguish open and closed sections. Subsequent sections are available after the reason, but heading plus disclosure creates more reader overhead. At 200%, collapsing the long reason requires returning to its top.

Strongest contextual decision flow: exact forecast, options, status and Save stay in reading order. Save needs scrolling at 200% but is fully shown at the bottom. Selected radio has a non-color cue. Saved text changes, while the unchanged Save label leaves completion slightly ambiguous.

All choices, status and Save fit together at 200%, giving the outcome step excellent scanability. However, the exact claim being judged is hidden behind View forecast. Saved feedback remains adjacent to Save, whose label does not change.

Exact forecast and fixed Save preserve context and action visibility. At 200%, the footer cuts across the options in selected/saved views; scrolling reveals them, but substantially less space remains for evaluating choices. Status is separated from the options by a large gap at normal size.

Strongest explanation of failure: unavailable, attempt used and tomorrow are explicit together. Orb retains prominence; full-width status avoids narrow wrapping. Expanded policy adds substantial scrolling at 200%, and its final line sits close to the tab bar. Touch the ball reads as an action despite the decorative prototype orb.

The status/Details split becomes a narrow, five-line status column at 200%, increasing scroll cost. Details is less informative than A's disclosure label. The focused policy sheet has readable full-width copy and a prominent Done button.

Most compact Home composition, with clean full-width wrapping and a readable policy sheet. However, Unavailable · try tomorrow looks like a retry destination rather than an explanation link. Used-attempt text is below the initial 200% viewport. Orb and tabs retain consistent visual roles.

reason: A best preserves the task's context: a focused long reader with an explicit return, the exact forecast beside its outcome choices, and a direct explanation of the unavailable omen. B's compact check-in and C's compact Home offer advantages, but conceal context or weaken destination clarity.
limitations: Scores are provisional judgments of supplied screenshots at normal and 200% text. Accessibility scores cover visible enlargement and layout only.
Reading-details feedback is null because screenshots establish content states, not navigation feedback or recovery behavior.
Check-in feedback scores assess visible selection and prototype-saved messages only; persistence and production success are unproven.
No interaction, target-size, contrast measurement, focus restoration, keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion or physical/native verification was performed.
Orb action, animation, real generation, model quality and production semantics are not established. Reported font/error/overflow checks were not independently repeated.
No composition demonstrates the required A≥9 and F≥9 threshold for every screen and meaningful component.
